title: Sandwich-like Microenvironments to Harness Cell/Material Interactions
protocol: Work in a fume hood.
Prepare a solution of 2% (w/v) PLLA in chloroform by stirring until completely dissolved at room temperature for approximately 3 hours.
Place stainless-steel washers on a glass Petri dish.
Add 200 µl of the PLLA solution into each washer.
Close the Petri dish with aluminum foil that has a few holes to allow slow evaporation of the solvent.
Evaporate solvent traces by heating samples at 120 °C for 5 minutes.
Allow samples to cool down at room temperature for approximately 30 minutes.
Cover cooled samples with 18.2 MΩ·cm water in the Petri dish and incubate for 8 minutes at room temperature.
Pry washers off the Petri dish using a razor blade.
Remove any imperfections from the edge of the washer with tweezers.
Let the samples air-dry.
Work in a fume hood.
Stir at room temperature until completely dissolved (approximately 3 hours) to prepare an 8% w/v PLLA solution in hexafluoroisopropanol.
Place polytetrafluoroethylene washers on an aluminum sheet or drum for electrospinning.
Load the syringe with the polymer solution and place it on a syringe pump.
Electrospin the PLLA solution using a flow rate of 0.9 ml/hr, voltage of 30 kV, and collector distance of 12 cm.
Stop the electrospinning process after 20-30 minutes once good fiber density is achieved.
Heat the samples at 120 °C for 5 minutes to evaporate solvent traces.
Store the PLLA samples in a vacuum desiccator (80 mbar) until the day of the experiment.
Work in a culture hood to ensure sterile conditions.
Sterilize all materials by UV exposure for 30 min.
Coat ventral and dorsal substrates with fibronectin at 20 µg/ml dissolved in DPBS containing Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ (200 µl/sample).
Incubate the samples in fibronectin solution for 1 hr.
Wash the samples twice with DPBS to remove excess protein.
Incubate samples in DPBS until use, using DPBS containing Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺.
Seed cells on the glass coverslips.
Seed C2C12 myoblast cells at 17,500 cells/cm² for differentiation experiments.
Seed NIH3T3 fibroblast cells at 7,000 cells/cm² for isolated cultures to study cell morphology and adhesion.
Place the samples in an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Allow cells to adhere to the ventral substrate for 3 hours.
Transfer the ventral seeded substrate into a new well of a 12 multi-well plate.
Overlay the dorsal substrate on the adhered cells carefully using tweezers.
Refill the well with medium (1 ml).
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Change the medium twice a week as in standard 2D cultures.
Work in a culture hood to ensure sterile conditions.
Sterilize all materials by UV exposure for 30 min.
Coat ventral and dorsal substrates with fibronectin in DPBS containing Ca2+ and Mg2+ at 20 µg/ml for 1 hr.
Wash samples twice with DPBS to remove excess protein.
Incubate samples in DPBS until use to prevent drying.
Seed cells on glass coverslips in a well of a 12 multi-well plate.
Overlay dorsal substrate on the seeded cells carefully using tweezers.
Refill with medium (1 ml) and incubate at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Change the medium twice a week as in standard 2D cultures.
Work in a culture hood to ensure sterile conditions.
Sterilize all materials by UV exposure for 30 min.
Coat the ventral substrate with fibronectin in 20 µg/ml dissolved in DPBS containing Ca2+ and Mg2+ for 1 hr.
Incubate the dorsal substrate with fibronectin in 20 µg/ml dissolved in DPBS containing Ca2+ and Mg2+ for 1 hr.
Wash the samples twice with DPBS to remove excess protein.
Incubate samples in DPBS until use to prevent drying.
Seed cells on glass coverslips at a high density.
Place the samples in an incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 until cells achieve confluence.
Use a pipette tip to scratch the cell monolayer, creating two populations separated by a gap.
Overlay the dorsal substrate onto the cells using tweezers and refill each well with medium (1 ml for a 12 multi-well plate).
Place the sample in a time-lapse microscope set to 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Take images of the gap closure every 20 minutes.
Analyze the gap closure using specific software such as MiToBo from ImageJ.
Prepare all buffers according to the manufacturer's instructions for commercial kits.
Remove culture media from samples in the sandwich-like cultures.
Wash the samples once with DPBS containing Ca2+ and Mg2+ (1 ml).
Remove all washing solution.
Remove the dorsal substrate using tweezers.
Add 350 μl of lysis buffer to the ventral substrate.
Overlay the dorsal substrate on the ventral substrate to lyse cells adhered to both substrates.
Isolate the lysis solution by removing the dorsal substrate.
Wash the sample once with DPBS.
Fix the sample with 4% formaldehyde in PBS for 20 min at 4 °C.
Rinse the sample with 1 ml of DPBS.
Permeabilize the sample with 0.5% Triton X-100 in DPBS (1 ml) for 5 min at room temperature.
Block non-specific binding sites with 1% albumin in DPBS (1 ml) for 30 min at room temperature.
Incubate the sample with primary antibody (2 μg/ml; 1 ml) in blocking solution for 3 hr at room temperature.
Wash the sample three times for 10 min each with DPBS/0.5% Tween 20 (1 ml).
Incubate the sample with secondary antibodies (2 μg/ml) and 1 μg/ml DAPI in blocking solution (1 ml) for 2 hr at room temperature.
Wash the sample three times for 10 min each in DPBS/0.5% Tween 20 (1 ml).
Wash in DPBS.
